answer: Before an agent may trade, it must pass New Zealand's RealMe verified identity: a passport or driver's licence checked in person at a PostShop, plus a photo matched to the document, so one verified identity maps to one real person. A forger needs a stolen passport, a faked photo match, and a physical visit for every fake — about 400 dollars and a fraud charge per identity — so a thousand fakes cost 400,000 dollars before earning a cent. One mismatch freezes the whole orchard of linked accounts, while the pulse of honest trade flows through opal-clear checks.
